title.narrative: Output 1.4. Increased capacity of Member States to improve social dialogue and labour relations laws, processes and institutions

description.narrative: 1. Ministry of Labour and Social Protection (MoLSP) developed an Electronic Case Management System (ECMS); a Systems for documentation and reporting of processes and outcome on workplace grievance handling mechanisms to be hosted by the Information and Communication Technology Authority under the Ministry of Communication] 2. Ministry of Labour and Social Protection (MoLSP) developed Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) regulations for the Labour and Industrial Relations Dispute Resolution in Tea and Textile Sectors and strengthened capacities of Conciliators/Mediators and MoLSP Secretariat on conciliation and mediation of labour disputes/ADR system 1. Utilizing resources availed under the USA, Department of Labor, Bureau for International Labor Affairs funded “All Hands in Kenya: Advancing Labour Standards through Cooperative Action” [KEN/20/01/USA], the ILO technically supported the designing and review of Electronic Case Management System (ECMS). The support entailed mapping and assessment of the standard operating procedures (SOPs) and workflows for labour inspection actions and institutional readiness of the Labour Inspectorate for an ECMS in October 2022. This was followed by the stakeholder workshops towards understanding of the need for an ECMS and co-creating the scope and functionality of the system in March 2023. The office is set to further support implementation the pending activities to build the ECMS on the wireframe and the Software Requirement Specifications (SRS) and train the Labour Inspectorate on the use of new ECMS, which is at procurement stage. 2. The ILO through the resources under the US funded project supported the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection (MoLSP) and social partners to develop Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) regulations, awaiting adoption. The office further embarked on the activities to strengthen capacities of Conciliators/Mediators and MoLSP Secretariat on conciliation and mediation of labour disputes and ADR system. This included a carrying out and validation of the findings of an assessment on access to judicial and non-judicial remedies. After, adoption of the new drafted ADR rules and regulations, the project plans to Partner with Kenya Judiciary Academy (KJA) and ITC-ILO to conduct training for judges, labour law practitioners on gaps identified and recommendations for institutions/mechanisms. Project has carried out and validated the findings of an assessment on access to judicial and non-judicial remedies

Output 7.4. Increased capacity of Member States to provide adequate labour protection to workers in diverse forms of work arrangements, including on digital labour platforms, and in informal employment

description.narrative: In September 2023, the government, in consultation with the social partners, validated a country-level diagnosis on the penetration of digital labour platforms across different sectors of the economy. The diagnosis documented the experiences of workers, with a focus on women in accessing and performing work on such platforms in the Kenyan economy, as well as the decent work deficits for women and men on digital labour platforms. The diagnosis was developed in consultation with social partners. The surveys were based on the sectors validated by the ILO’s tripartite constituents in September 2021. The sectors included location-based domestic and beauty work, personal services, healthcare and medical consultation, tutoring, and taxi and delivery platforms; online freelance and microtask platforms; e-commerce platforms and BPO companies. With support from the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation (BMGF), ILO conducted a survey of 1,028 workers across the identified sectors of the Kenyan economy and also conducted key informant interviews with representatives of governments, trade unions, employers’ organizations and platform companies to capture their perspectives, particularly regarding public policies frameworks to promote decent work in the platform economy. The country-level diagnosis serves to build capacities of the ILO’s tripartite constituents regarding the penetration of digital labour platforms across various sectors of the economy and understand the opportunities and challenges for workers on these platforms. The diagnosis will contribute towards developing a holistic approach in addressing issues related to working conditions of workers working on digital the ongoing as well as BPO companies. The opportunities and challenges highlighted from the survey findings will feed into the discussions on the ‘Digital labour policy’, which is under discussion in Kenya. Efforts are being made to have a Joint Task Force with all the stakeholders to discuss various safeguards to protect the workers, and the diagnosis will serve as a basis for this discussion. Finally, it will also help towards formulating job creation policies in Kenya, in light of the increasing educated youth unemployment in the country who are engaged in micro task and freelance academic writing tasks.

description.narrative: The Ministry of Labour and Social Protection led by the labour inspectorate departments adopted and commenced implementation of a Strategic Compliance Plan developed by a tripartite plus Strategic Compliance Task Team (SCTT) in March 2023. This will ensure optimal use of resources to enforce compliance with the International Labour Standards and Acceptable Conditions of Work. With the resources from the US funded project; All Hands in Kenya: Advancing Labour Standards through Cooperative Action. The ILO provided technical support o the Strategic Compliance Task Team (SCTT) in the development of a Strategic Compliance Plan. The support entailed Strategic Compliance Plan (SCP) workshops conducted in July 2022, in which 32 participants (12 female and 20 male) drawn from Labour department (14) Directorate of Occupational Safety and Health Services (DOSHS), (12), Central Organization of Trade Unions Kenya, COTU (K), (1), Federation of Kenya Employers (2) Judiciary (1), Kenya Tea Growers Association (KTGA) and The Export Processing Zones Authority (EPZA) were trained and supported formation of a Strategic Compliance Task Team (SCTT). The office also supported a meeting of the Strategic Compliance Task Team (SCTT) to review the Strategic Compliance Plan in March 2023.
